documents.title: GenAI Syllabus Statements
documents.stance_why: The page says "Instructors at the University may allow or prohibit the use of Generative AI" and "Use of generative artificial intelligence as part of coursework requires written instructor permission". It sets no uniform allow or ban and supplies two templates for instructors to adapt, so it delegates and lists the templates as tiers.
tiers: AI Use is Prohibited (sample syllabus statement)
AI Use Is Permitted (sample syllabus statement)
documents.summary: Provost guidance on syllabus statements for GenAI. It lists required and optional statements and gives two sample templates (prohibited, permitted), with a university default that unauthorized GenAI use is scholastic dishonesty.

units.why: Opening sentence says "Instructors at the University may allow or prohibit the use of Generative AI", so the university sets no single rule and leaves the choice to each instructor: P04 (per-instructor rule), actor instructor, informs.
units.anchor: Instructors at the University may allow or prohibit the use of Generative AI (GenAI) tools

units.why: "strongly encouraged to include a clear syllabus statement outlining their expectations" asks instructors to put AI expectations in the syllabus, which is P09; a recommendation, so should.
units.anchor: strongly encouraged to include a clear syllabus statement outlining their expectations

units.why: "A well-crafted course policy should define acceptable and unacceptable uses of GenAI, reference relevant academic policies" specifies what the syllabus policy must contain, so P09 (the syllabus statement requirement) fits better than P04.
units.anchor: should define acceptable and unacceptable uses of GenAI, reference relevant academic policies

units.why: "Students should consult their instructors if they are unsure what constitutes acceptable use" is an ask-first rule, P10, addressed to students.
units.anchor: Students should consult their instructors if they are unsure what constitutes acceptable use

units.why: The sentence says "developed in collaboration with the Senate Committee on Educational Policy", stating how the guidance was made: P84.
units.anchor: developed in collaboration with the
units.fit_note: Only names the co-developing body; no date or consultation process.

units.why: Statement 1 says "Use of generative artificial intelligence as part of coursework requires written instructor permission": by default AI is barred unless an instructor permits it, i.e. a fallback/default permission rule (P06) rather than P01 because permission can be granted.
units.anchor: Use of generative artificial intelligence as part of coursework requires written instructor permission

units.why: "Provide specific examples of how students may or may not use GenAI tools" tells instructors to make their rules concrete in the syllabus: P09.
units.anchor: Provide specific examples of how students may or may not use GenAI tools

units.why: "Encourage students to consult and confirm the policy before starting an assignment" asks students to check before beginning work: P10, addressed to instructors to prompt.
units.anchor: Encourage students to consult and confirm the policy before starting an assignment

units.why: Statement 2 tells instructors to "Clearly state whether UMN-licensed Generative AI tools are permitted in the course, even if GenAI use is prohibited"; it is a syllabus-content requirement about tools (P09), with tool naming not fully captured.
units.anchor: Clearly state whether UMN-licensed Generative AI tools are permitted in the course
units.fit_note: Specifically about stating which AI tools (esp. UMN-licensed ones) are allowed, even under a ban.

units.why: "Instructors are encouraged to recommend UMN-licensed tools" nudges instructors to point students to the university-licensed tools: P92 (institution-wide licensed tools), not P17 because it is not course-specific.
units.anchor: Instructors are encouraged to recommend UMN-licensed tools

units.why: "these have been vetted for accessibility and data privacy" gives the reason for preferring licensed tools, matching P50 (prefer vetted tools, protect data).
units.anchor: these have been vetted for accessibility and data privacy

units.why: "available to students at no cost through their UMN login" is an access/cost statement: licensed tools are free to students, P51.
units.anchor: available to students at no cost through their UMN login

units.why: "Third-party tools that fall outside the University’s licensing agreements may not meet these standards, though students may choose to access them independently" warns about unvetted tools but allows independent use; P92 is the nearest.
units.anchor: Third-party tools that fall outside the University’s licensing agreements may not meet these standards
units.fit_note: Also states students may still choose third-party tools on their own.

units.why: "Faculty interested in purchasing licenses for third-party tools are encouraged to consult" the software purchase request process: this routes tool acquisition through institutional review, P65.
units.anchor: Faculty interested in purchasing licenses for third-party tools are encouraged to consult

units.why: "Generative AI tools are considered online learning support platforms and may not be used for course assignments except as explicitly authorized by an instructor" is the default ban-unless-authorized rule, P06.
units.anchor: may not be used for course assignments except as explicitly authorized by an instructor

units.why: The quoted Regents definition lists "the unauthorized use of online learning support and testing platforms" as scholastic dishonesty, so AI misuse is treated as academic misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: including the unauthorized use of online learning support and testing platforms
units.frag_end: approved for the specific course in question;

units.why: The Grading policy "provides instructors the discretion to award a grade of an F or N" for scholastic dishonesty: a stated sanction, P37.

documents.title: Teaching with Generative AI
documents.stance_why: The page is a resource hub ("key resources ... on how to best incorporate generative AI") with no rule for or against AI use, and it points to the Senate syllabus statements and examples from "AI-prohibitive to using AI to augment learning", so decisions sit with instructors.
documents.summary: Teaching Support landing page that lists resources: AI-literacy courses for students and instructors, syllabus statement examples, tool guidance and campus-specific pages. It states little policy itself.

units.why: Describes GenAI+U as equipping "UMN students with the knowledge, skills, and ethical understanding" for responsible AI use: university AI-literacy training, P70.
units.anchor: equips UMN students with the knowledge, skills, and ethical understanding necessary

units.why: The instructor guide is "a guide for University of Minnesota instructors to navigate the transformative role of Generative AI in education": faculty learning support, P63.
units.anchor: a guide for University of Minnesota instructors to navigate the transformative role of Generative AI
units.frag_end: simply wish to better understand their impact on instruction.

units.why: The assessment resource "outlines essential considerations for using GenAI for classroom assessment", advice for instructors weighing AI on student work: P63 (faculty advice), as P101 would need explicit conditions.
units.anchor: outlines essential considerations for using GenAI for classroom assessment
units.fit_note: Resource on whether and how to use AI on student work, without stating conditions.

units.why: The academic-integrity course "covers student engagement strategies, AI detection tools, citation practices, assignment design, and steps for responding to potential misuse": faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: covers student engagement strategies, AI detection tools, citation practices, assignment design

units.why: "Example syllabus statements on the use of AI in academic classes, developed by the Senate Committee on Educational Policy" points instructors to sample statements: P09 is nearest.
units.anchor: Example syllabus statements
units.fit_note: Resource link offering sample statements; it does not itself require a syllabus statement.

units.why: "Examples demonstrating the spectrum of GenAI usage in (or not) in coursework (from AI-prohibitive to using AI to augment learning)" shows that courses range from ban to integration: P04.
units.anchor: Examples demonstrating the spectrum of GenAI usage in (or not) in coursework

units.why: Writing Across the Curriculum guides on "Strategies for incorporating GenAI" and "Strategies for restricting GenAI use" offer both directions: P04.
units.anchor: Strategies for restricting GenAI use in courses with writing

units.why: "Learn how to leverage approved generative AI tools to support student learning" points to guidance for university-approved tools: P92.
units.anchor: Learn how to leverage approved generative AI tools to support student learning

units.why: "Campus or College Specific Teaching Resources" lists separate LATIS, CEHD, UMD and graduate-school pages, so units publish their own guidance: P85.
units.anchor: Campus or College Specific Teaching Resources
units.fit_note: Lists units with their own guidance; no statement that units may set additional rules.

units.why: The IT appropriate-use page is described as "about acceptable use of tools AI tools by all University members", pointing to the university framework: P56.
units.anchor: about acceptable use of tools AI tools by all University members

units.why: "introduces some of the ethical issues and other risks that AI tools like ChatGPT present" names ethical concerns: P53.
units.anchor: introduces some of the ethical issues and other risks that AI tools like ChatGPT present

units.why: Navigating AI @UMN "brings together resources for faculty, staff, and students to responsibly leverage, and innovate with, AI": an institution-wide hub, P56.
units.anchor: to responsibly leverage, and innovate with, AI in academic, research, and professional endeavors

units.why: The student tutorial "was created to provide tools to be an effective, ethical, and responsible user of GenAI" and instructors "may wish to share" it: AI training for students, P70.
units.anchor: was created to provide tools to be an effective, ethical, and responsible user of GenAI
units.frag_end: share this resource with their students.

units.why: The Libraries video "briefly covers how AI works, how (and if) you can use AI for your research, plus some major concerns": AI literacy for undergraduates, P70.
units.anchor: how AI works, how (and if) you can use AI for your research

units.why: The AI iCoP is "an informal group discussing Artificial Intelligence" open to staff, faculty and students: a community for learning about AI, P63 (not faculty-only, but nearest).
units.anchor: an informal group discussing Artificial Intelligence
units.fit_note: Open to staff and students as well as faculty.

units.why: The fellows program aims "to foster a multidisciplinary learning community that uses generative AI in teaching practice and to promote the effective use and best practices": faculty community, P63.
units.anchor: to foster a multidisciplinary learning community that uses generative AI in teaching practice
units.frag_end: best practices of this emerging technology.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence: Appropriate Use of Generative AI Tools
documents.stance_why: The page encourages licensed tools ("OIT encourages the use of UMN-Licensed tools") and allows AI use under data, IP and contract conditions, e.g. "Safeguarding data means only uploading allowed University data into appropriately licensed tools". Student coursework use is left to instructors, but the page overall permits with conditions.
documents.summary: IT guidance on appropriate use of generative AI tools covering data classification, licensed versus unlicensed tools, ethics, IP and licensing, contracts, and role-specific duties for students, staff, faculty and service owners.

units.why: Opening says AI is changing teaching and that "it is crucial to understand how to safeguard data and use them appropriately": sets purpose of the page, P56.
units.anchor: it is crucial to understand how to safeguard data and use them appropriately

units.why: "All people who use AI ... are responsible for understanding the policies that support and enable data and information security, ethics, and legal compliance" requires awareness of existing policy: P77.
units.anchor: responsible for understanding the policies that support and enable data and information security

units.why: "Data classified as Public data can be used freely in generative AI platforms" permits public data in any AI tool: P50 (data rules).
units.anchor: Data classified as Public data can be used freely in generative AI platforms

units.why: "In all cases, use must be consistent with the University’s Data Security Classification policy" binds AI use to existing policy: P77.
units.anchor: use must be consistent with the University’s

units.why: "Safeguarding data means only uploading allowed University data into appropriately licensed tools" restricts what data goes to which tools: P50.
units.anchor: only uploading allowed University data into appropriately licensed tools

units.why: "The table below outlines the data types you can and can’t add to AI tools" gives a tool-by-data-class table (e.g. no Highly Restricted data in ChatGPT Edu): P50.
units.anchor: data types you can and can't add to AI tools
units.fit_note: A tool-by-data-class matrix; the anchor only introduces it.

units.why: "Your department or unit may have additional restrictions" says units can add rules: P85.
units.anchor: Your department or unit may have additional restrictions

units.why: "OIT encourages the use of UMN-Licensed tools" recommends the licensed tools: P92.
units.anchor: OIT encourages the use of UMN-Licensed tools

units.uncovered_note: Users must apply the university's ethical decision-making values when using AI.

units.why: "all software is subject to the review process for software purchases, including the vendor review process" requires review of any AI tool, paid or free: P65.
units.anchor: all software is subject to the review process for software purchases

units.why: "Students must understand instructor expectations. This is paramount." makes students responsible for knowing each instructor’s rules: P78.
units.anchor: Students must understand instructor expectations. This is paramount.

units.anchor: review guidelines for new AI functionality when enabling or adding them to their tools
